I am 63 years old and I have farmed my 6 mu of land here in Quzhou County my whole life. My family’s plot is on the North China Plain, and the soil is good for the wheat-maize rotation my father taught me. My winter wheat went into the ground last October—same as every year—after I rotary-tilled the soil and broadcast a compound fertilizer as basal dressing. Now that the growing season is starting, I will irrigate the wheat three or four more times from my well: the winter irrigation is already done, but I still need to water at green-up, jointing, and grain-filling. I will topdress with urea twice and spray for weeds, aphids, and rust—maybe three or four applications in total. I expect about 1000 jin per mu, give or take the weather. Come early June, as soon as the wheat is harvested, I will immediately plant summer maize. I will buy hybrid seed—Denghai 605 or Nongda 372, whatever the supply shop has—because hybrids give better yields. I will not till for the maize; there is no time between crops and diesel is expensive, so I direct-seed into the wheat stubble with a no-tillage planter. I will put down compound fertilizer at sowing and irrigate twice during the summer if the rains are not enough. The maize will need a herbicide at planting and a couple of insecticide sprays later. I reckon I can get about 1100 jin per mu of maize. I do not grow cotton or vegetables anymore—they need too much labor and my son works in Shijiazhuang now. Wheat and maize are stable: the grain buyers come right to the village edge, and I can store some for family flour and feed. At my age, with middle schooling, I trust what I know, and this rotation has never failed to put food on the table.
